raw_response:
I've been farming these 3 mu for 30 years, and my wife and I manage everything ourselves. We don't hire labor — can't afford it, and anyway 3 mu is small enough that we can handle it between the two of us. We're tight on cash, so I can't just do what the extension office recommends. I listen to them, sure, but then I do what my wallet and my experience allow.

**Wheat:** I'll plant the whole 3 mu in winter wheat, probably around October 10th. I've been saving seed from my own crop for two years, but last autumn the germination looked a bit off, so this year I'll buy fresh improved seed — about 7.5 kg per mu, costs roughly 25 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, the extension guy says 18 kg nitrogen per mu, but that's too expensive for me. I'll put down 40 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base before planting, which gives about 6 kg each of N, P, and K. Then at jointing in March, I'll topdress with 15 kg of urea, adding another 7 kg of nitrogen. That brings me to about 13 kg N per mu total. It's not optimal, but last year I did about the same and got 400 kg per mu, which is acceptable. I might throw another 5 kg of urea at heading if the crop looks yellow and I have a little extra cash, but I'm not counting on it. I'll irrigate three times — once before winter or at green-up, once at jointing, and once at heading. Each irrigation costs about 35–40 yuan per mu with the pump meter, so I have to be careful. I'll spray herbicide in early spring and keep an eye out for aphids; if they show up, I'll spray insecticide too.

**Maize:** The wheat comes off around June 8th, and I have to get the maize in the ground within two or three days — the window is brutally tight. No time for deep plowing. I'll do a quick rotary till or just plant into the wheat stubble if the soil is soft enough. Maize has to be hybrid seed, so I buy it every year — about 2 kg per mu, costs around 45 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, I'll apply 35 kg of compound (15-15-15) at planting, and then topdress with 15 kg urea when the plants reach the big trumpet stage in July. That's roughly 12 kg N per mu. I'll irrigate twice — once right after planting if it hasn't rained, and once at silking in late July. Three times would be better, but the pumping costs add up. I'll put down herbicide at planting and spray for corn borer once in July if I see moths or damage.

**Tradeoffs:** Every yuan I spend on wheat fertilizer is a yuan I don't have for maize seed or irrigation. My neighbor with 8 mu can afford 20 kg N per mu and gets 500 kg, but I can't copy him — I have less land and less cash. I'd rather apply a little too much fertilizer than too little, because a bad year hurts more than a good year helps, but "too much" has a hard limit at what I can pay. We rely entirely on family labor — my wife and I can just manage the 3 mu, but if one of us gets sick, we're in trouble.

I know the extension recommendations, but I can't afford them, so I apply moderate fertilizer — enough to avoid a big yield drop but not enough to optimize. I irrigate wheat three times because that's what everyone does and the crop needs it, but I limit maize to two irrigations to save on pumping costs. I buy hybrid maize seed every year but use improved wheat seed that I refresh every few years. My target yields are conservative: 400 kg/mu for wheat and 450 kg/mu for maize.
